resources.string: The short version: BurnPony has no accounts, collects nothing about you, runs no analytics, and the relay cannot read your notes. Here is the long version.
This policy covers the BurnPony apps, the note-viewing pages at burnpony.app, and the website — all developed and operated by NorseHorse, an independent developer. Contact: NorseHorse@norsehor.se

Nothing about you. There is no account, no sign-up, and the app never asks for your name, email address, or contacts. The Sent tab keeps a local record of the notes you have created: the note ID, a management token, your chosen settings, the status the app has fetched back (views used, whether it burned, receipt times) and your optional device-local label. That record exists only on this device.

The note text is not kept unless you turn on Saved copies in Settings, and even then only for notes where you switch on Keep a copy. Each copy is encrypted to a key held in this phone\'s secure hardware (Android Keystore, StrongBox where available), which only uses the key after your fingerprint, face or screen lock. The key never leaves the device and is never backed up or synced, so a copy cannot be opened anywhere else, or by the app itself without that unlock. Double bottom notes are never saved. You can delete a copy at any time or have copies delete themselves after 7, 30 or 90 days, and removing a note from the Sent tab removes its copy. Saved copies are never sent to the relay.

Notes are stored on a relay so recipients can fetch them. For each live note the relay holds:

• The sealed envelope — your note, encrypted on this device with AES-256-GCM. The decryption key travels only in the link's # fragment, which browsers do not send to servers, so the relay cannot read the note. Even the auto-hide setting travels encrypted inside it.

• Bookkeeping — a random note ID, created and expiry timestamps, the view allowance and count, whether a read receipt was requested, and a hash of the management token used for early burn.

• Receipt times — if and only if you enabled receipts for that note, the times it was opened.

• Push registrations — device push tokens (up to five per note) so your phone can receive the generic "A note was opened." notification. They are removed with the note.

Ciphertext is deleted in the same database transaction as the last allowed view, at expiry (a sweep runs every five minutes), or when you burn the note early. Burned, expired, and never-existed notes return identical responses.

To keep the relay healthy, note creation and abuse reports are rate-limited using IP addresses hashed with a server-side secret; those hash records expire after roughly two hours. Like any internet server, the relay sees connecting IP addresses at the network level while handling a request; it does not build profiles from them, and the web server in front of it is configured with access logging disabled.

The viewer includes a report function. A report stores the note ID, the reason text the reporter enters (up to 500 characters), and the reporting time, for operator review. Reports are purged after 30 days, and submitting one never reveals whether a note exists.
There is no analytics SDK, no advertising SDK, and no crash reporter that transmits your data. Nothing is sold or shared with anyone.

Note ciphertext lives exactly as long as its view allowance and expiry allow, and not a sweep-cycle longer. Receipt records and push registrations are removed with their note. Rate-limit hashes expire in about two hours; abuse reports in 30 days. Deleting the app deletes your local Sent records; because there is no account, there is no server-side profile to delete.
BurnPony is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect information from anyone, children included.
If this policy changes, the update appears here and on the website with a new date. There is no dark-pattern re-consent flow because there is no data collection to consent to.
By using the BurnPony app, relay, or website you accept these terms. BurnPony is operated by NorseHorse, an independent developer.

BurnPony provides self-destructing notes: text encrypted on your device, stored temporarily as ciphertext on a relay, and delivered through a shareable link. Notes are removed once their view allowance or expiry is reached. The service is currently provided free of charge.

Use BurnPony in accordance with the laws that apply to you. Do not use it for harassment, threats, fraud, or to distribute illegal content, and do not attempt to disrupt or overload the relay. The viewer includes an abuse reporting mechanism; reported notes may be removed, and note creation is rate-limited.

A note link — plus its passphrase, if you set one — is the sole means of reading a note. Anyone who receives the link can read the note until it burns or expires. Lost links cannot be restored, regenerated, or recovered by anyone, including the developer.
Notes are designed to be irrecoverable once they burn or expire. Do not use BurnPony as storage for anything you need to keep. Deleted ciphertext cannot be restored by anyone.

BurnPony is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind, express or implied. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the developer is not liable for service interruptions, lost notes, or any damages arising from use of the service.

The relay holds encrypted notes temporarily and may be changed, moved, or taken offline to maintain the service. If you point the app at your own self-hosted relay in Settings, that relay is yours to operate and these terms do not govern it.
Updates to these terms appear here and on the website with a revised date. Continued use after a change means you accept it.
